facts.statement: The type specimen of Ingentia was discovered in the Quebrada del Barro Formation in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Ingentia, PVSJ 1086, was discovered in the Quebrada del Barro Formation of northwestern Argentina.

facts.statement: Ingentia was described in 2018 by a team led by Cecilia Apaldetti and colleagues.
facts.quote: It was described in 2018 by Cecilia Apaldetti, Ricardo Nestor Martínez, Ignacio Alejandro Cerda, Diego Pol and Oscar Alcober

facts.statement: The fossils of Ingentia were discovered in May 2015 by Diego Abelín and the paleontology team of the UNSJ Institute and Museum of Natural Sciences.
facts.quote: Su descubrimiento fue realizado en mayo de 2015 por Diego Abelín y el equipo de paleontología del Instituto y Museo de Ciencias Naturales de la UNSJ.

facts.statement: The remains were exhumed from the Balde de Leyes site in the Caucete department, southeast of San Juan province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Sus restos fueron exhumados en un yacimiento ubicado en la zona de Balde de Leyes, en el departamento Caucete, al sudeste de la provincia de San Juan, centro-oeste de la Argentina.

facts.statement: Ingentia lived during the Late Triassic (late Norian-Rhaetian) in Argentina.
facts.quote: Ingentia is a genus of early sauropodiform dinosaur, sometimes considered a basal sauropod, from the Late Triassic (late Norian-Rhaetian) of Argentina.

facts.statement: Ingentia was a large herbivorous sauropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Fue un dinosaurio saurópodo herbívoro de gran tamaño.

facts.statement: Adult Ingentia specimens are estimated to have reached lengths of 8 to 10 meters and weighed nearly 10 tonnes.
facts.quote: Se calculó que en vida los ejemplares de esta especie medían entre 8 y 10 metros de longitud y pesaban cerca de 10 toneladas.

facts.statement: The discovery of Ingentia suggests that gigantism evolved approximately 30 million years earlier than previously thought, before the appearance of the first eusauropods.
facts.quote: Su hallazgo permitió descubrir que el fenómeno del gigantismo se adelantó algunos 30 millones de años antes de lo que se postula, hace 180 millones de años, con la aparición de los primeros eusaurópodos.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Ingentia in the family Lessemsauridae, a clade that also includes Lessemsaurus and Antetonitrus.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis performed by Apaldetti et al. found a new clade uniting Ingentia, Lessemsaurus and Antetonitrus, which they named Lessemsauridae.

facts.statement: Like other lessemsaurids, Ingentia possessed highly pneumatic dorsal and cervical vertebrae, short but tall robust cervical vertebrae, a widely expanded distal scapula blade, and upright arms.
facts.quote: Como otros lessemsáuridos, Ingentia tenía sus vértebras dorsales y cervicales sumamente neumatizadas, vértebras cervicales anteroposteriores cortas pero muy altas, cervicales robustas, una escápula muy extendida en su extremo distal, y brazos erguidos.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the clade containing Ingentia represents the oldest sauropod taxon or the sister group to Sauropoda, depending on how Sauropoda is defined.
facts.quote: Depending on the definition of Sauropoda, the clade is either the oldest sauropod taxon, or the sister taxon of the clade Sauropoda.

facts.statement: The name Ingentia prima was chosen to reference the large body size acquired during the early evolution of dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Mediante esta combinación se deseó hacer alusión al gran tamaño corporal adquirido durante la evolución temprana de los dinosaurios.
